content: Estriol, also known as oestriol, is one of the three primary estrogens produced by the human body. It is synthesized in significant amounts only during pregnancy, as it is produced by the placenta. Research conducted at UCLA's Geffen Medical School has demonstrated that estriol can significantly alleviate symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in pregnant women. In non-pregnant women, estriol levels remain relatively stable after menopause and are not significantly different from the levels observed in men. Estriol levels can be measured to assess the overall health of a developing fetus. Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S), which is produced by the fetal adrenal cortex, is converted into estriol by the placenta. If the levels of unconjugated estriol are abnormally low in a pregnant woman, this may indicate potential developmental issues in the fetus. Estriol measurement is included as part of the triple test, a prenatal screening tool.
